   City Council Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, July 16, 2019

   CALL TO ORDER
   PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Vice Mayor Menchaca
   ROLL CALL: Mayor Pu, Vice Mayor Menchaca, Council Members Costanzo,
  Harrington, Liao

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. RECOGNITION OF LA GARDENIA MEAT MARKET, SAN GABRIEL

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  This is the time set aside for members of the public to address the City Council on
  items of interest that are not on the Agenda, but are within the subject matter
  jurisdiction of the San Gabriel City Council. Pursuant to the Brown Act, the City
  Council cannot answer any questions or take any action until such time as the
  matter may appear as an item on a future agenda.

  In an effort to provide everyone with an opportunity to speak tonight, please be
  aware that all public comments will be limited to a maximum of three minutes. You
  will receive a 30-second warning as you approach the end of your time. As a
  reminder, please be respectful of all speakers regardless of the position they take
  on any items.

  If you wish to address the City Council, please complete a speaker’s request card
  and hand it to the clerk before the start of the meeting. When speaking, please
  state your NAME for the record.

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 16, 2019  2
   1. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of July 2, 2019.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of June 25, 2019.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  This is the presentation of the “Register of Demands and Warrants” for the
  payment of City expenditures.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – JUNE 2019

  This is a presentation of City investments for the month of June 2019.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  D. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 19-32 APPROVING A PROPOSITION 68
  GRANT APPLICATION AND ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 19-34 TO
  AMEND THE 2019-20 OPERATING BUDGET

  The City of San Gabriel has the opportunity to apply for grant funds through
  Statewide Park Development and Community Revitalization Program, funded
  through Proposition 68. This program will award over $650 million in multiple
  rounds of funding. Grants will be awarded on a competitive basis for the
  creation of new parks and new recreation opportunities in proximity to the most
  critically underserved communities across California. All projects must create or
  renovate at least one recreation feature. The City intends to apply for Statewide
  Park Program funding for the renovation of Smith Park and Smith Park Pool.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 19-32 approving the City’s application for grant funds
  through the Proposition 68 Statewide Park Development and Community
  Revitalization Program; and
  2. Adopt Resolution No. 19-34 appropriating $28,750 from Development
  Impact Fees into account number 124-850-40-96-814 for the grant
  expenses.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 16, 2019  3
   E. RESOLUTION NO. 19-28 FOR TEMPORARY STREET CLOSURE AT 864
  COMMERCIAL AVENUE BETWEEN GLADYS AVENUE AND THE RUBIO
  WASH ON JULY 27, 2019

  The Public Works Department received a request from Ogopogo Brewing
  Company for a temporary street closure for a promotional event on Saturday,
  July 27, 2019 from 2:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. on Commercial Avenue between
  Gladys Avenue and the Rubio Wash. Resolution No. 19-28 details the location,
  date, and times for the closure, as well the conditions that must be followed by
  the applicant. The Public Works Department, Fire Department and Police
  Department have reviewed and approved the request.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-28 authorizing
  closure of Commercial Avenue between Gladys Avenue and the Rubio Wash
  from 2:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. on Saturday, July 27, 2019.

  F. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 19-29 AMENDING THE 2019-20
  OPERATING AND CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM BUDGETS AND
  APPROVAL OF PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH JMDIAZ,
  INCORPORATED FOR CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT AND INSPECTION
  OF THE TRAFFIC SIGNAL INSTALLATION AT SAN GABRIEL BOULEVARD
  AND COMMERCIAL AVENUE

  The project will construct a new traffic signal at the intersection of San Gabriel
  Boulevard and Commercial Avenue. The traffic signal design and construction
  was a condition of approval for the mixed-use project at 402-404 South San
  Gabriel Boulevard. The design was completed in 2013. The developer placed
  deposits with the City for the construction. On March 21, 2019, three bids were
  received and publicly opened. Comet Electric Incorporated, is the lowest
  responsible bidder, with a bid of $218,575. The total amount of Comet Electric
  Incorporated’s bid, including two additive bid items, is $245,879. During the
  July 2, 2019, City Council Meeting, the City Council directed staff to provide an
  explanation of the two additive items that were added to the construction
  contract, and to bring this Construction Management contract item back to the
  City Council for approval.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Adopt Resolution No. 19-29 appropriating $27,755 in Measure R Funds; and

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 16, 2019  4
   2. Approve the Professional Services Agreement with JMDiaz, Incorporated
  and authorize the City Manager to execute said Agreement not to exceed
  $27,755 (including 10% contingency in the amount of $2,523) for
  construction management and inspection for the traffic signal installation
  at San Gabriel Boulevard and Commercial Avenue; and
  3. Approve a Purchase Order in the amount of $27,755 from account number
  122-800-58-97-280.

  G. AMENDMENT TO PROFESSIONAL SERVICE AGREEMENT WITH CIVIL
  WORKS ENGINEERS FOR THE GREAT STREETS PROGRAM

  On June 20, 2017, the City Council approved a Professional Services Agreement
  with Civil Works Engineers to provide engineering design services for the Great
  Streets Program and approved a purchase order in the amount of $320,327. On
  November 21, 2017, the City Council approved Amendment No. 1 to the
  agreement with Civil Works Engineers to include additional streets in the design
  and approved an increase of $73,115 to the agreement for a new total not to
  exceed amount of $393,442. The additional services are necessary due to a
  change of design at Junipero Place, two additional bulb out curb ramps on
  Santa Anita Street, and an extension of the pavement limits on Santa Anita
  Street to Mission Road.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Amendment No. 2 with Civil
  Works Engineers, Inc. and approve an increase to Purchase Order No. 7737 in
  the amount of $21.225 from account number 122-800-41-97-704, for a total
  agreement amount of $414,667.

  H. REVOCABLE LICENSE AGREEMENT WITH YZL INVESTMENT, LLC FOR USE
  OF PARKING SPACES AT THE MISSION DISTRICT PARK & RIDE LOT (257
  SOUTH MISSION DRIVE)

  In this proposed action, the City is acting in its proprietary capacity as the owner
  of the Mission District Park & Ride Lot located on the westerly side of Mission
  Drive, adjacent to the former Mission 261 Restaurant. The property and
  business owner of the former Mission 261 Restaurant – YZL Investment, LLC –
  together with its prospective tenant, have applied for a Conditional Use Permit
  to open a new restaurant. They approached the City to request use of the
  Mission District Park & Ride Lot to satisfy the minimum off-street parking
  requirement for a limited time. The proposed restaurant would need
  approximately 50 spaces; the total lot contains approximately 111 parking
  spaces. Based on direction from Council, this Revocable License Agreement

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 16, 2019  5
   with YZL Investment provides a two-year term commencing today, and gives
  the City Manager authority to extend it for one year. This arrangement is
  intended to protect the City’s freedom to make long-term decisions involving
  the Park & Ride Lot. The $1,000-per-month License Fee commences only if the
  proposed restaurant is issued a certificate of occupancy.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the License Agreement with
  YZL Investment.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. PUBLIC HEARING – ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 19-31 TO UPDATE
  THE CITY’S CITYWIDE (MASTER) FEE SCHEDULE

  Staff requests that the Public Hearing be opened and continued to the August
  20, 2019 Regular City Council Meeting.

 6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. PROJECT PREVIEW: SELF-STORAGE FACILITY (PLANNED DEVELOPMENT
  (PD), DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT (DA), TENTATIVE PARCEL MAP (TPM),
  AND PRECISE PLAN OF DESIGN (PPD)) AT 414 SOUTH SAN GABRIEL
  BOULEVARD
  PLANNING CASE NO. PD19-001
  APPLICANT: 1784 CAPITAL HOLDINGS, LLC

  The subject property is located on the east side of South San Gabriel Boulevard
  between Commercial Avenue (to the south) and Broadway (to the north). The
  proposed project would require the assembly of eleven parcels which are
  located in between San Gabriel Boulevard (to the west) and Gladys Avenue (to
  the east). There are currently six buildings on the proposed project site, which
  total approximately 11,579 square feet (SF). This is preview of a pending
  application and involves no substantive discussion or decision-making. All
  information provided is tentative and subject to change.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review and file the staff report.

  B. ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT UPDATE

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 16, 2019  6
   The economic development presentation is intended to provide the City
  Council information on current industry trends to help grow the local economy.
  Additionally, the presentation will serve as an update on the City’s Economic
  Development program and priorities for the coming year.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Update.

 7. PUBLIC COMMENT

 8. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

 9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

 10. CLOSED SESSION – None.

 11. ADJOURNMENT

  Due to the observance of National Night Out on August 6, 2019, the next regular
  City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, August 20, 2019 at 6:30 p.m. in the
  Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California.
  Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will be available
  on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website at
  www.sangabrielcity.com.
